newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend
in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday
unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Aston Villa (7) v Sunderland (11)
Trinidadian Dwight Yorke missed his second penalty in a
month as Villa lost 1-0 at home to Sheffield Wednesday in
mid-week and once title challengers Villa have only one win in
nine games and will miss midfielders Ian Taylor (thigh) and
captain Andy Townsend (shoulder) again.
Sunderland are away for the second time in four days after
drawing 1-1 at Leicester on Wednesday. Welsh defender Andy
Melville suffered a broken nose but will play and midfielder
Darren Williams could retain his place after scoring. Manager
Peter Reid's attempts to sign Rennes defender Allan Johnston
have been upset by his former Scottish club Hearts taking an
interest in the deal.
Blackburn Rovers (16) v West Ham United (18)
These two sides will be hoping to recover after midweek
losses to Tottenham and Arsenal respectively. Blackburn received
a double boost when goalkeeper Tim Flowers and defender Graeme
Le Saux were recalled to the England squad for the World Cup
qualifier against Italy on February 12.
Troubled West Ham manager Harry Redknapp looks set to
strengthen his attack by signing Paul Kitson from Newcastle next
week. West Ham are in the relegation zone having won just one of
their last 16 matches.
Derby County (15) v Liverpool (3)
Derby and Liverpool will both be aiming to rediscover
winning form. Derby could see the return of striker Dean
Sturridge after he missed the midweek goalless draw at Leeds
with a hamstring injury. Croatian defender Igor Stimac is
expected to return in two weeks after a hernia operation while
striker Ashley Ward will be out for another month with a leg
injury.
For Liverpool, Irish defender Phil Babb and midfielder
Michael Thomas return after their two-game suspensions and their
only doubt is defender Neil Ruddock with a hamstring injury.
Everton (12) v Nottingham Forest (17)
Nottingham Forest will want to recover quickly from their
midweek defeat at Coventry, their first after five successive
victories, and pull struggling Everton into the relegation
battle.
Everton will be out to prevent a club record after equalling
the club's worst sequence when they fell to their sixth
consecutive league defeat at Newcastle in midweek. Manager Joe
Royle expects defender Craig Short to recover from slight
concussion received in that 4-1 defeat. Royle expects midfielder
Joe Parkinson, who returned after a long injury absence, to keep
his place in an unchanged squad.
Forest duo Dean Saunders and Brian Roy both have outside
chances of recovering from hamstring injuries. Paul McGregor
could make a return after suffering knee and ankle injuries at
the beginning of the season.
Leeds United (10) v Arsenal (2)
Defender David Wetherall returns for George Graham's Leeds
after a two-match suspension and goalkeeper Nigel Martyn is also
set to return after missing the midweek game with a back injury.
Leeds have kept nine clean sheets in their last 13 games, but
come up against the premier league's top scorer Ian Wright with
17. Defender Martin Keown and Dutchman Dennis Bergkamp will both
be missing for a second time through suspension.
Manchester United (1) v Southampton (19)
Alex Ferguson saw his side move top of the table for the
first time this season with a 2-1 victory over Wimbledon on
Wednesday when defender Gary Pallister and England midfielder
David Beckham returned from injury.
Southampton were knocked out of the League Cup 2-1 by
Stockport County of the second division on the same night and
could be suffering a crisis of confidence. Dutch defender Claus
Lundekvam and forward Matthew Oakley are both doubtful with
thigh and ankle injuries. Midfielder Robbie Slater and defender
Francis Benali are suspended and manager Graeme Souness faces
mounting problems for their most difficult fixture of the
season, but will draw strength from the memory of their 6-3 home
win over United earlier this season.
Sheffield Wednesday (8) v Coventry (14)
Coventry manager Gordon Strachan's only change from his
winning side is likely to be new 2.5 million pounds ($4 million)
signing Gary Breen who could make his debut in defence to
replace Liam Daish who is ruled out for the season through
injury.
Wednesday have lost only once in their last 16 games.
Defender Jon Newsome could return after a stomach bug while
Italian Benito Carbone (groin) is still doubtful.
Tottenham Hotspur (9) v Chelsea (6)
England midfielder Darren Anderton returned briefly in
Tottenham's 2-1 victory against Blackburn, but Swiss
international defender Ramon Vega sustained a hamstring injury.
Vega will miss this London derby and will be out for a month
with the injury in which time he will serve a three-match ban
for his sending-off at Forest. Scottish international defender
Colin Calderwood is suspended while strikers Chris Armstrong and
Teddy Sheringham are still injured.
Chelsea will be high on confidence after coming back from
two goals down to defeat Liverpool 4-2 in the F.A. Cup last
weekend.
Wimbledon (5) v Middlesbrough (20)
Wimbledon manager Joe Kinnear hopes his side can bounce back
from their defeat by Manchester United to further
Middlesbrough's relegation worries. Kinnear has the same squad
to choose from while Middlesbrough coach Bryan Robson has
several worries.
Midfielder Craig Hignett is out with a calf strain while
defender Curtis Fleming (knee) and midfielder Phil Stamp
(hamstring) are doubtful.
On Sunday, 1600 GMT:
Newcastle United (4) v Leicester City (13)
Kenny Dalglish could start with Colombian Faustino Asprilla
after his impressive display in the 4-1 win against Everton.
England striker Les Ferdinand took a knock on his knee in that
game, but should be available while Belgian defender Philippe
Albert is in contention after recovering from a hamstring
injury.
